content:
#2 That’s the Brown representability theorem: Whitehead-generalized cohomology theories are those whose classifying spaces are (stages of) spectra.

So this doesn’t even need sheaves yet. If one does add sheaves to this picture, one gets Whitehead-generalized differential cohomology theories (differential K-theory, etc.)

Some survey of this and related facts in the hom-space perspective on cohomology is in Section 2 (pp. 9) of The Character Map in Twisted Non-Abelian Cohomology
subject: Generalized cohomology as sheaf cohomology?

content:
#4 Let’s introduce some notation to make this clearer:

By

KU0 ≃ Z×BU ≃ ʃFred  ∈  Grpd∞ \mathrm{KU}_0 \,\simeq\, \mathbb{Z} \times B U \,\simeq\, ʃ \mathrm{Fred} \;\in\; \mathrm{Grpd}_\infty KU0​≃Z×BU≃ʃFred∈Grpd∞​

one means the bare homotopy type of the classifying space for complex K-theory.

So for XXX any topological space with ʃX ∈ ʃ X \,\in\,ʃX∈ Grpd∞\mathrm{Grpd}_\inftyGrpd∞​ its underlying homotopy type, we have that the K-theory of XXX is (the homotopy type of) the mapping space (I am using notation as on pp. 37 of arXiv:2008.01101 and pp. 6 in arXiv:2112.13654):

K(X)  =  KU0(X)  ≃  π0Maps(ʃX, KU0) . K(X) \;=\; \mathrm{KU}^0(X) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{Maps}\big( ʃ X,\, \mathrm{KU}_0 \big) \,. K(X)=KU0(X)≃π0​Maps(ʃX,KU0​).

No sheaves so far. And this generalizes: For every Whitehead-generalized cohomology theory EEE there is a spectrum E∙E_\bulletE∙​ such that (assume XXX is compact, if you like)

E0(X)  ≃  π0Maps(ʃX, E0) . E^0(X) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{Maps}\big( ʃ X,\, E_0 \big) \,. E0(X)≃π0​Maps(ʃX,E0​).

No sheaves have been invoked anywhere yet. This all happens in the classical homotopy category.

But now assume that XXX is equipped with the structure of a smooth manifold. This canonically makes it an object in the cohesive ∞\infty∞-topos

SmthGrpd∞  ≔  Sh∞(CartSp) \mathrm{SmthGrpd}_\infty \;\coloneqq\; \mathrm{Sh}_\infty\big( \mathrm{CartSp}\big) SmthGrpd∞​:=Sh∞​(CartSp)

of smooth ∞\infty∞-groupoids.

The shape modality

ʃ   ⁣:  SmthGrpd∞→    Shp    Grp∞↪    Dsc    SmthGrpd∞ ʃ \;\colon\; \mathrm{SmthGrpd}_\infty \xrightarrow{ \;\; \mathrm{Shp} \;\; } \mathrm{Grp}_\infty \xhookrightarrow{ \;\; \mathrm{Dsc} \;\; } \mathrm{SmthGrpd}_\infty ʃ:SmthGrpd∞​Shp​Grp∞​Dsc​SmthGrpd∞​

still remembers the underlying bare homotopy type ʃXʃ XʃX of XXX, but XXX is much richer now.

In particular, there exists a sheaf of spectra KU^∙ ∈ Spectra(SmthGrp∞)\widehat {\mathrm{KU}}_\bullet \,\in\, \mathrm{Spectra}\Big(\mathrm{SmthGrp}_\infty\Big)KU∙​∈Spectra(SmthGrp∞​) whose shape, in turn, is still the plain classifying homotopy type from above

ʃKU^∙  ≃  KU∙ , ʃ \widehat {\mathrm{KU}}_\bullet \;\simeq\; \mathrm{KU}_\bullet \,, ʃKU∙​≃KU∙​,

but which represents differential K-theory K^(X)\widehat{K}(X)K(X) in that

K^(X)  =  KU^0(X)  ≃  π0ʃMaps(X, KU^0)  ≃  π0SmthGrp∞(X, KU^) . \widehat{K}(X) \;=\; \widehat{\mathrm{KU}}{}^0(X) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 ʃ \mathrm{Maps}\big( X ,\, \widehat{\mathrm{KU}}_0 \big) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{SmthGrp}_\infty\big( X ,\, \widehat{\mathrm{KU}}\big) \,. K(X)=KU0(X)≃π0​ʃMaps(X,KU0​)≃π0​SmthGrp∞​(X,KU).

Here on the right we have the shape of the mapping stack, equivalently the ∞\infty∞-categorical hom-space of smooth ∞\infty∞-groupoids.

More generally, for every spectrum E∙E_\bulletE∙​ one may find a sheaf of spectra E^∙ ∈ Spectra(SmthGrp∞)\widehat{E}_\bullet \,\in\, \mathrm{Spectra}\big( \mathrm{SmthGrp}_\infty \big)E∙​∈Spectra(SmthGrp∞​) such that

E^0(X)  ≃  π0ʃMaps(X, E^0)  ≃  π0SmthGrpd(X, E^0) \widehat{E}{}^0(X) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 ʃ \mathrm{Maps}\big( X,\, \widehat{E}_0 \big) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{SmthGrpd}\big( X,\, \widehat{E}_0 \big) E0(X)≃π0​ʃMaps(X,E0​)≃π0​SmthGrpd(X,E0​)

is a corresponding differential cohomology.

Finally, to actually answer your last question: The plain cohomology is still available in the differential context:

E0(X)  ≃  π0SmthGrpd∞(X, ʃE^0)  ≃  π0Grpd∞(ʃX, E0) . E^0(X) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{SmthGrpd}_\infty\big(X,\, ʃ \widehat{E}_0 \big) \;\simeq\; \pi_0 \mathrm{Grpd}_\infty\big( ʃX,\, E_0 \big) \,. E0(X)≃π0​SmthGrpd∞​(X,ʃE0​)≃π0​Grpd∞​(ʃX,E0​).

Here the term in the middle may be understood as forming the sheaf hypercohomology of XXX with coefficients in the locally constant ∞\infty∞-stack ʃE^0ʃ \widehat{E}{}^0ʃE0.

For more on all this see also the differential cohomology hexagon.

For a quick but complete account of the actual technical details see pp. 106 and then pp. 65 in arXiv:2009.11909.

(Of course all this is also in dcct (schreiber), but the above references are more polished.)

content:
#6

  1. Does any Whitehead-generalized cohomology theory EEE has a differential version (i.e. a corresponding sheaf of spectra in Spectra(SmthGrp∞)\mathrm{Spectra}(\mathrm{SmthGrp}_{\infty})Spectra(SmthGrp∞​)?

Oh yes, all of them do. Under mild conditions there is a canonical such, in general there are many. Lecture notes include Section 4 “Differential extensions of generalized cohomology theories” (pp. 71) in Uli Bunke’s arXiv:1208.3961.

In the previous sentence, what are all of the other known variations of SmoothGrpd ∞SmoothGrpd_{\infty} for the (generalized) cohomology theories to extend?

Here I am not sure if I understand what you have in mind. Do you mean differential cohomology in ∞\infty∞-toposes other than that of smooth ∞\infty∞-groupoids? In that case, one answer is:

Yes, this holds whenever there is an analog of the Poincaré-lemma/de Rham theorem. Namely, this enters in constructing a differential cohomology theory in “Hopkins-Singer style” (referring to Hopkins and Singer 2005, which started the topic) as a homotopy fiber product of a bare spectrum (over its Chern-Dold character) with the sheaf of de Rham complexes valued in a chain complex model for the real-ification of the spectrum (e.g. Example 4.29 on p. 68 here).

For example, one can use complex analytic ∞-groupoids. The differential Whitehead-generalized cohomology theories in this case were discussed already in Quick & Hopkins arXiv:1212.2173.
